summary: Plan grilled against the roadmap acceptance criteria, accepted decisions 0118/0119, and the architecture/lessons. Every task traces to a criterion; the smaller alternatives (agent-fork, session-only, agent-global grants) are recorded as rejected decisions rather than silently dropped. Schema, acting-identity, and the recurring delivery-semantics class each carry an explicit mitigation.
gaps: Risk of over-building by forking a separate agent/persona per DM.
Schema change to agent_tool_bindings could drift if done as raw SQL rather than through the canonical repository.
Acting-identity could be resolved on a path that never threads personId, silently dropping a person's grant.
Task 5's in-group acknowledgement touches the RECURRING delivery-semantics class at jobs/execution-readiness (x3, SETUPRACE-1).
Task write-scopes must stay disjoint so workers do not collide.
resolutions: Agent-fork refuted in decision 0118 and listed as a non-goal; per-person isolation reuses the shipped personId memory boundary — no fork, no routing/brain change, no migration.

Schema goes through the canonical Drizzle repository with repository tests and an architecture-map/docs update (Technical Approach + Risks + Tests row; lessons schema-storage, canonical-postgres-cutover).
Acting-identity read is centralised in resolveAgentToolRuntimePolicy and fails closed (grant simply doesn't apply) if personId is absent; the job and live-turn paths are explicitly tested (Risks).
Explicit tripwire recorded: if review flags delivery-semantics on the ack path, escalate per WORKFLOW.md Recurring Findings rather than patch again (Risks).
Decomposition splits tasks 1-4 (authority+grant foundation, one PR) from task 5 (installer onboarding, own PR), keeping write scopes disjoint.
open_items: Person-scoped credentials, alias-verification gating, and the full org governance tier are deferred (D-0054) — non-blocking for these acceptance criteria.
